title: AI Food and Drink Videos With a Fresh Pour | AIVideosUGC
description: Make AI food and drink videos from a single bottle or can photo: a slow pour, ice, and fizz in a 9:16 clip for TikTok and Reels. Upload your photo to start.
h1: Make AI Food and Drink Videos From a Bottle Photo
lead: AI food and drink videos turn a photo of your bottle or can into a close-up pour with ice, bubbles, and fresh fruit. Get a 6, 10, 15, or 30 second vertical clip made for scrolling feeds.
intro: A quick, close-up pour is the whole idea: your drink flowing from bottle to glass. The sample shows sparkling orange juice splashing over ice next to a sliced orange, with whole fruit on a cutting board behind it.

Pour shots show color, fizz, and texture in a couple of seconds, which is what stops a thumb mid-scroll. Use it for juices, sodas, cold brew, kombucha, sauces, or syrups. A 6-second clip is plenty for a TikTok or Reels ad, while 10 seconds leaves room for a slower pour and a final look at the full glass.
tip: Upload a photo with the bottle upright and the liquid color visible, then mention the glassware, the ice, and what sits on the counter.

steps.d: A straight-on photo lets the video carry the shape and liquid color into the pour.
Describe the glass, garnish, and surface, like "tall glass, crushed ice, lime wedge, marble counter." Pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.
Add flavor names, prices, and sound in Canva or CapCut, since letters in AI video can come out garbled.

ideas.d: Swap the orange slice for berries or a cinnamon stick when a new seasonal flavor comes out.
Try honey over pancakes, hot sauce over tacos, or syrup swirling into iced coffee.
Make a 1:1 version to sit next to your still photos in a Shopify product gallery.

faq.q: What kinds of drinks work with this?
faq.a: Anything you pour: juice, soda, sparkling water, iced tea, cold brew, and mixers. Clear glass bottles and bright liquids tend to look the most striking.

faq.q: Will my label come out clearly?
faq.a: Small print may not be perfect. Keep the label facing the camera in your photo, and if the brand name needs to be crisp, add it as text in your editing app.

faq.q: How long should a pour video be?
faq.a: Six seconds covers a single pour and loops nicely in a feed. Choose 10 seconds if you want a slower pour plus a moment on the finished glass.
